rules: 252-day windows on fundamentals (leverage delta, book_per_share/close, roa mean) caused all 3 coverage rejects this round (0.871-0.872 vs 0.90 needed). Keep fundamental-field windows at 126 days or less unless coverage is confirmed first.

A rank-difference between a value signal (earnings yield) and short-term momentum (10-day mean return) scored far above everything else this round (fitness 7.07 vs next-best 0.82). This value-minus-momentum rank structure is worth extending with other value/momentum field pairs.

Pure fundamental-ratio transforms with no market-based term (margin/turnover/roe-roa spread, asset_turnover delta, eps-delta over book_per_share) were the weakest cheap_screen rejects (|t| 0.31-0.70). Fundamentals alone are not clearing the screen this round.

Pairing a fundamental with a return-based term did better but still missed once: roa times EMA(return,60) reached |t| 0.85, the closest cheap_screen miss. Refine the return-term side (different smoothing or window) rather than abandoning this pairing direction.
Very short deltas (5-day) on slow-moving fundamentals (accrual_gap) scored among the weakest (|t| 0.55). Slow-moving fields need longer differencing windows to carry signal.

Five of fifteen rejects duplicated 9 to 15 nodes of one already-archived stochastic-range / dollar-volume-range subtree. That lineage is saturated; branch into new structural forms instead of recombining it further.

A bare field proposed next to its own rank transform ($roa vs RANK($roa)) is a near-guaranteed correlation reject (rho about 1.0). Changing only the wrapper around an already-archived field is not a new signal.
One reject used plain RANK instead of CS_RANK on a 252-day roa mean. Verify cross-sectional operators are applied consistently so rejections reflect true signal quality, not an operator slip.
